Calculation methodology & sources ›

Evidence, not promises

The simulation runs the inspected public browser module 90218.G, with the original hero, item, counter, synergy and economy data. Server settings and ranked parity have not been verified. It never sends a match to your DotaCaptain account.

The seed comes from hero IDs and your side. Repeating identical inputs produces the same result; repeated wins would not establish confidence.

The optional example catalogue tests 240 drafts against Early aggression, Late split and Teamfight / Rosh on Radiant and Dire. Equal win counts are sorted by mean final net worth lead. These six correlated scenarios are a stress test, not a statistical sample.

General ranking & counter search

General ranking uses 256 stratified profiles: all 64 enemy strategies under two lineup policies, on both sides. Two seeded 128-profile replications each cover all 64 plans under both lineup policies. Shortlists do not react to the evaluated team. Common seeds and rules are used across candidates; exclusions can require different legal lineups. Equal policy weights are a benchmark assumption, not observed opponent frequencies. Subgroup wins and replication ranks expose sensitivity. The optional Solo-doctrine sort reweights the same results using the public 97174.R0 generator: its unique base presets and 0/1/2-axis flips. Under uniform random draws, flip counts have weights 35%, 48.75%, and 16.25%. Enemy hero selection remains hypothetical; this is not an actual Solo win probability. The 512 weighted results and replication rank ranges are neither real win probabilities nor confidence intervals. Duplicate cases retain scenario weights; unique cases are reported.

Current-draft scope constrains hypothetical completions to revealed heroes and supplied scout axes. General optimization screens 64 own plans on 16 training profiles, refines the best eight plus the current plan on 128 training profiles, then evaluates the selected plan on a separate evaluation seed bank (256 profiles by default). Evaluation never selects the plan; overlap is disclosed when known inputs collapse scenarios. The shortlist can miss the best plan. Unknown roles vary across legal preferred-role assignments. Detail pages show three strongest distinct opponent lineups found in that suite. Deeper counter search screens up to 36 lineups across three plans, then tests all 64 plans for the four strongest screened lineups, keeping your displayed configuration fixed and testing both sides. It is a bounded search, not a proof of the globally best counter. Ban priorities count how many found threats contain a hero; banning it blocks those exact lineups, not every replacement.

Native formulas & optimization

Native draft value is the arithmetic mean of five scores from DotaCaptain’s original AI pick formula (module 16286), with each hero in its assigned role alongside the other four heroes. Role fit, doctrine, composition, counters, synergies, timing, redundancy and comfort retain the original coefficients and caps. The mean is our catalogue aggregation, not an official team score. No account comfort history is supplied.

Search samples 6,000 role-valid lineups and improves 20 candidates through single-role replacements. The search reserves candidates for eligible carries, mids and offlaners, then fills up to 120 rows by score. New searches return an untested native-score shortlist; benchmark testing and optimization are explicit batch actions. All 64 plans are screened for each shortlisted draft. Single-match optimization tests all 64 plans exactly for that supplied matchup. General optimization uses the training shortlist and separate evaluation above. Neither establishes a global optimum. Alternatives keep the current plan and need a fresh simulation.

Items use the role-aware default presets from the DotaCaptain draft page, in their original order. Item editing and optimization are outside this initial version. Test all 64 strategies runs the simulation for your selected matchup with these fixed defaults. Baseline differences compare native draft points against a configuration explicitly selected by you; no baseline is selected automatically. Live pick/ban suggestions run the native AI decision function on the confirmed picks and bans; opponent replies remain uncertain. Ranked server profiles, organization modifiers and live server settings are unavailable.
